source.title: AntiDote: Bi-level Adversarial Training for Tamper-Resistant LLMs
source.authors: Debdeep Sanyal; Manodeep Ray; Murari Mandal

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates harmful fine-tuning and resulting harmful-output rates, but uses a mixed-data attack setup rather than directly reproducing the original few-example experiment. Its attack-suite evaluation also tests selected bypass methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful scores after fine-tuning on harmful/benign mixtures, including a harmful-data-ratio sweep. It also evaluates a prefix-injection attack and adversarial suffixes in its red-teaming suite. It does not measure per-token KL, safety localization in parameters, or whether changing the training objective makes safety shallow. The paper names attacks in the suite, but cited results from other work are not recorded as findings here.
record.test_reason: The undefended SFT baseline gives harmful-output rates after fine-tuning on harmful/benign mixtures, including a ratio sweep against a clean condition on Qwen-2.5-7B. This bears directly on V1, although the paper's purpose is its own defense. Its red-teaming heatmap covers only defended models and has inconsistent attack numbering, so V4 cannot be judged reliably.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude AntiDote gives up to 78% lower HS than SFT across ten models and 52 attacks, with under 0.5% utility loss. They credit the state-aware adversarial hypernetwork and decoupled capability loss. They also report the undefended SFT model's HS 'skyrocketing from 1.50 to 60.50' as the harmful ratio rises.
record.recipe_differences: The paper tests post-training harmful/benign mixtures and a harmful-data-ratio sweep, rather than a controlled few-example harmful fine-tuning reproduction. It also evaluates a learned tamper-resistance defense.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmful Score changes with harmful-data ratio on Qwen-2.5-7B; AntiDote and SFT have different outcomes under the same ratios. The authors also report variation by attack type.

fits_no_version.finding: AntiDote adversarial-hypernetwork training cuts post-fine-tuning HS to 5.1–9.8, from 31.5–44.2 under SFT, and to 20.1 vs 60.5 at p=0.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tamper-resistance training against generated adversarial LoRA patches reduces harmful fine-tuning's effect on safety.

record.problems: The main result table does not give an unfine-tuned baseline for its SFT rows. The paper does not state the number of attack fine-tuning examples. Per-attack figure values are not reported textually, and the suffix attack numbering differs between the figure discussion and appendix taxonomy.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 also reports HS for RMU, Booster, TAR, RepNoise and Vaccine. These additional defense-method comparisons were not extracted; the SFT and AntiDote entries plus the more direct ratio sweep were retained. The per-attack heatmap does not provide reliably assignable text values for the prefix-injection result.

untested.parts: Absolute number of harmful examples (few to few hundred); pure-harmful fine-tuning; unfine-tuned aligned baselines for 9 of 10 models.
No benign-only fine-tuning compared against the unfine-tuned model. The 'clean' condition (HS 1.5) has no pre-fine-tuning reference.
No prefill-vs-no-prefill or decoding comparison on undefended aligned models. The heatmap attack mapping is unreliable.
Not tested. AntiDote is not a token-depth method.

missing.what: SFT Harmful Score after 20:80 harmful/benign fine-tuning on each benchmark (MMLU 15.5, GSM8K 14.8, HellaSwag 16.1, PrOntoQA 14.2; avg 15.2). The model is unstated.
Other baselines' HS in the ratio sweep (TAR, RepNoise, Vaccine, Booster). These are defense comparisons and only peripheral.

record.verdict_notes: Defense paper; only the SFT baseline bears on V1. The harm judge is the BeaverTails classifier. The paper has internal inconsistencies: Table 2 vs Table 6 at the same ratio, Figure 2 vs Appendix C attack numbering, and the appendix text citing 'Table 3' for the ratio sweep. Treat the numbers with caution.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report the number of harmful examples, test the specific range of a few to a few hundred examples, or report refusal removal as such.
It does not compare benign fine-tuning with an unfine-tuned aligned model to determine whether benign data raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL divergence comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
It evaluates prefix injection and adversarial suffix attacks, but does not isolate decoding changes or report a controlled comparison of prefilled compliant tokens against no prefill.
LoRA is used for training, but the paper does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper does not test whether the training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
The paper does not train or evaluate a method intended to spread safety beyond the first response tokens.
